name: What is the difference between a recessed beam and a dropped beam?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a recessed beam and a dropped beam?

acceptedAnswer.text: A hidden beam is recessed directly into the ceiling joists for a flat, seamless ceiling, while a dropped beam hangs below the ceiling surface. A flush, recessed beam creates an uninterrupted sightline across the room, which is ideal for modern open-concept renovations. However, recessing requires cutting existing ceiling joists, hanging them from the new beam with joist hangers, and ensuring clear attic or joist clearance above. A dropped beam is installed directly underneath the existing joists, which makes installation simpler and less labor-intensive, but leaves a visible, boxed-in header running across the ceiling.
acceptedAnswer.description: A recessed beam sits flush inside the ceiling for a seamless look, while a dropped beam rests below ceiling level and remains visible as a finished header.
